005package org.wpilib.system;
006
007import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Amps;
008import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Celsius;
009import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Nanoseconds;
010import static org.wpilib.units.Units.Volts;
011
012import java.util.function.LongSupplier;
013import org.wpilib.hardware.bus.CANPort;
014import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.HAL;
015import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.HALUtil;
016import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.PowerJNI;
017import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.can.CANJNI;
018import org.wpilib.hardware.hal.can.CANStatus;
019import org.wpilib.units.measure.Current;
020import org.wpilib.units.measure.Temperature;
021import org.wpilib.units.measure.Time;
022import org.wpilib.units.measure.Voltage;
023
024/** Contains functions for roboRIO functionality. */
025public final class RobotController {
026  private static LongSupplier m_timeSource = RobotController::getMonotonicTime;
027
028  private RobotController() {
029    throw new UnsupportedOperationException("This is a utility class!");
030  }
031
032  /**
033   * Return the serial number of the roboRIO.
034   *
035   * @return The serial number of the roboRIO.
036   */
037  public static String getSerialNumber() {
038    return HALUtil.getSerialNumber();
039  }
040
041  /**
042   * Return the comments from the roboRIO web interface.
043   *
044   * <p>The comments string is cached after the first call to this function on the RoboRIO - restart
045   * the robot code to reload the comments string after changing it in the web interface.
046   *
047   * @return the comments from the roboRIO web interface.
048   */
049  public static String getComments() {
050    return HALUtil.getComments();
051  }
052
053  /**
054   * Returns the team number configured for the robot controller.
055   *
056   * @return team number, or 0 if not found.
057   */
058  public static int getTeamNumber() {
059    return HALUtil.getTeamNumber();
060  }
061
062  /**
063   * Sets a new source to provide the clock time in nanoseconds. Changing this affects the return
064   * value of {@code getTime} in Java.
065   *
066   * @param supplier Function to return the time in nanoseconds.
067   */
068  public static void setTimeSource(LongSupplier supplier) {
069    m_timeSource = supplier;
070  }
071
072  /**
073   * Read the nanosecond timestamp. By default, the time is based on the monotonic clock. However,
074   * the return value of this method may be modified to use any time base, including non-monotonic
075   * and non-continuous time bases.
076   *
077   * @return The current time in nanoseconds.
078   */
079  public static long getTime() {
080    return m_timeSource.getAsLong();
081  }
082
083  /**
084   * Read the nanosecond timestamp. By default, the time is based on the monotonic clock. However,
085   * the return value of this method may be modified to use any time base, including non-monotonic
086   * and non-continuous time bases.
087   *
088   * @return The current time in a measure.
089   */
090  public static Time getMeasureTime() {
091    return Nanoseconds.of(m_timeSource.getAsLong());
092  }
093
094  /**
095   * Read the nanosecond monotonic timer.
096   *
097   * @return The current monotonic time in nanoseconds.
098   */
099  public static long getMonotonicTime() {
100    return HALUtil.getMonotonicTime();
101  }
102
103  /**
104   * Read the nanosecond monotonic timer in a measure.
105   *
106   * @return The current monotonic time in a measure.
107   */
108  public static Time getMeasureMonotonicTime() {
109    return Nanoseconds.of(HALUtil.getMonotonicTime());
110  }
111
112  /**
113   * Read the battery voltage.
114   *
115   * @return The battery voltage in Volts.
116   */
117  public static double getBatteryVoltage() {
118    return PowerJNI.getVinVoltage();
119  }
120
121  /**
122   * Read the battery voltage in a measure.
123   *
124   * @return The battery voltage in a measure.
125   */
126  public static Voltage getMeasureBatteryVoltage() {
127    return Volts.of(PowerJNI.getVinVoltage());
128  }
129
130  /**
131   * Gets a value indicating whether the FPGA outputs are enabled. The outputs may be disabled if
132   * the robot is disabled or e-stopped, the watchdog has expired, or if the roboRIO browns out.
133   *
134   * @return True if the FPGA outputs are enabled.
135   */
136  public static boolean isSysActive() {
137    return HAL.getSystemActive();
138  }
139
140  /**
141   * Check if the system is browned out.
142   *
143   * @return True if the system is browned out
144   */
145  public static boolean isBrownedOut() {
146    return HAL.getBrownedOut();
147  }
148
149  /**
150   * Gets the number of times the system has been disabled due to communication errors with the
151   * Driver Station.
152   *
153   * @return number of disables due to communication errors.
154   */
155  public static int getCommsDisableCount() {
156    return HAL.getCommsDisableCount();
157  }
158
159  /**
160   * Gets the current state of the Robot Signal Light (RSL).
161   *
162   * @return The current state of the RSL- true if on, false if off
163   */
164  public static boolean getRSLState() {
165    return HAL.getRSLState();
166  }
167
168  /**
169   * Gets if the system time is valid.
170   *
171   * @return True if the system time is valid, false otherwise
172   */
173  public static boolean isSystemTimeValid() {
174    return HAL.getSystemTimeValid();
175  }
176
177  /**
178   * Get the input voltage to the robot controller.
179   *
180   * @return The controller input voltage value in Volts
181   */
182  public static double getInputVoltage() {
183    return PowerJNI.getVinVoltage();
184  }
185
186  /**
187   * Get the input voltage to the robot controller in a measure.
188   *
189   * @return The controller input voltage value in a measure.
190   */
191  public static Voltage getMeasureInputVoltage() {
192    return Volts.of(PowerJNI.getVinVoltage());
193  }
194
195  /**
196   * Get the voltage of the 3.3V rail.
197   *
198   * @return The controller 3.3V rail voltage value in Volts
199   */
200  public static double getVoltage3V3() {
201    return PowerJNI.getUserVoltage3V3();
202  }
203
204  /**
205   * Get the voltage in a measure of the 3.3V rail.
206   *
207   * @return The controller 3.3V rail voltage value in a measure.
208   */
209  public static Voltage getMeasureVoltage3V3() {
210    return Volts.of(PowerJNI.getUserVoltage3V3());
211  }
212
213  /**
214   * Get the current output of the 3.3V rail.
215   *
216   * @return The controller 3.3V rail output current value in Amps
217   */
218  public static double getCurrent3V3() {
219    return PowerJNI.getUserCurrent3V3();
220  }
221
222  /**
223   * Get the current output in a measure of the 3.3V rail.
224   *
225   * @return The controller 3.3V rail output current value in a measure.
226   */
227  public static Current getMeasureCurrent3V3() {
228    return Amps.of(PowerJNI.getUserCurrent3V3());
229  }
230
231  /**
232   * Enables or disables the 3.3V rail.
233   *
234   * @param enabled whether to enable the 3.3V rail.
235   */
236  public static void setEnabled3V3(boolean enabled) {
237    PowerJNI.setUserEnabled3V3(enabled);
238  }
239
240  /**
241   * Get the enabled state of the 3.3V rail. The rail may be disabled due to a controller brownout,
242   * a short circuit on the rail, or controller over-voltage.
243   *
244   * @return The controller 3.3V rail enabled value
245   */
246  public static boolean getEnabled3V3() {
247    return PowerJNI.getUserActive3V3();
248  }
249
250  /**
251   * Get the count of the total current faults on the 3.3V rail since the code started.
252   *
253   * @return The number of faults
254   */
255  public static int getFaultCount3V3() {
256    return PowerJNI.getUserCurrentFaults3V3();
257  }
258
259  /** Reset the overcurrent fault counters for all user rails to 0. */
260  public static void resetRailFaultCounts() {
261    PowerJNI.resetUserCurrentFaults();
262  }
263
264  /**
265   * Set the voltages where the robot will enter and recover from brownout.
266   *
267   * <p>The brownout voltage must be between 5 V and 8 V, inclusive. The recovery voltage must be no
268   * greater than 8.5 V and at least 0.5 V above the brownout voltage.
269   *
270   * @param brownoutVoltage the voltage where the robot will enter brownout
271   * @param recoveryVoltage the voltage where the robot will recover from brownout
272   */
273  public static void setBrownoutVoltages(double brownoutVoltage, double recoveryVoltage) {
274    PowerJNI.setBrownoutVoltages(brownoutVoltage, recoveryVoltage);
275  }
276
277  /**
278   * Set the voltages in measures where the robot will enter and recover from brownout.
279   *
280   * <p>The brownout voltage must be between 5 V and 8 V, inclusive. The recovery voltage must be no
281   * greater than 8.5 V and at least 0.5 V above the brownout voltage.
282   *
283   * @param brownoutVoltage the voltage where the robot will enter brownout
284   * @param recoveryVoltage the voltage where the robot will recover from brownout
285   */
286  public static void setBrownoutVoltages(Voltage brownoutVoltage, Voltage recoveryVoltage) {
287    PowerJNI.setBrownoutVoltages(
288        brownoutVoltage.baseUnitMagnitude(), recoveryVoltage.baseUnitMagnitude());
289  }
290
291  /**
292   * Get the current CPU temperature in degrees Celsius.
293   *
294   * @return current CPU temperature in degrees Celsius
295   */
296  public static double getCPUTemp() {
297    return PowerJNI.getCPUTemp();
298  }
299
300  /**
301   * Get the current CPU temperature in a measure.
302   *
303   * @return current CPU temperature in a measure.
304   */
305  public static Temperature getMeasureCPUTemp() {
306    return Celsius.of(PowerJNI.getCPUTemp());
307  }
308
309  /**
310   * Get the current status of the CAN bus.
311   *
312   * @param busId The bus ID
313   * @return The status of the CAN bus
314   */
315  public static CANStatus getCANStatus(CANPort busId) {
316    CANStatus status = new CANStatus();
317    CANJNI.getCANStatus(busId.value, status);
318    return status;
319  }
320}
